column1: # How each sub-test ROM in this directory was built, and -- since 2026-09-19 --
# WHICH CATALOG ENTRY EACH ONE ACTUALLY RUNS, measured rather than inferred.
# A sub-test ROM is the FULL AccuracyCoin ROM with its boot path patched to
# enter one catalog entry directly, produced by
# `scripts/accuracycoin-build/build_sub_test_rom.py <src> --suite S --test T`.
# `suite` is the 0-based offset into `TableTable` in AccuracyCoin.asm and
# `test` the 0-based row within that suite -- NOT the catalog's flat order.
# THE INDICES ADDRESS THE BUILD EMBEDDED IN THE ROM, NOT UPSTREAM TODAY. That
# is the whole difficulty, and it is why the 31 legacy rows sat empty for four
# releases. Each ROM carries its own copy of the assembly, so `--suite 18
# --test 2` means whatever `TableTable[18][2]` was in the source it was built
# from. Upstream has since reordered its suites AND inserted tests inside them,
# so both obvious ways to recover a legacy ROM's identity give a wrong answer,
# confidently:
#   * against the CURRENT assembly (46199ae4), `ppu-misc-stale-bg-shift-regs`
#     (enc 18/2) resolves to `$2002 flag timing`;
#   * against the STALE suite map kept struck through in the builder's
#     docstring, the same ROM resolves to `INC $4014`.
# It is neither. The ROM writes `$0483`, which is `Stale BG Shift Registers` --
# the test its filename names. Both routes are inference; the ROM was asked
# instead.
# THE `result_addr` COLUMN IS THE IDENTITY, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT.
# `subtest_identify` (crates/rustynes-test-harness/src/bin) boots each ROM,
# runs it, and reports which byte in `$0400-$04FF` it writes. A result address
# is the catalog's own key and is stable across upstream reorderings, so it
# needs no suite map at all. The CONTROL is that
# `RustyNES_MiSTer/tb/regress.sh` independently registers eighteen of these
# ROMs by an address it read out of golden RAM during v2.6.4/v2.6.5: all
# eighteen come back identical. `enc_suite`/`enc_test` are recorded beside it
# as a fingerprint of the file -- they pin the bytes, not the meaning.
# `tests/accuracycoin_subtest_provenance.rs` re-measures every row and fails on
# any disagreement, so a swapped, rebuilt or renamed ROM is caught rather than
# trusted. Regenerate the data rows with:
#   cargo run -p rustynes-test-harness --release --features test-roms \
#     --bin subtest_identify -- --tsv tests/roms/AccuracyCoin/sub-tests/*.nes
# THREE THINGS THE MEASUREMENT FOUND, none of which reading the filenames could
# have:
#   * `ppu-misc-2004-stress.nes` does NOT run `$2004 Stress Test`. It writes
#     `$048E`, which is `$2007 Stress Test` -- the same entry as
#     `ppu-misc-2007-stress.nes`. So the corpus has two ROMs for one entry and
#     NO ROM for `$2004 Stress Test` ($048C), while appearing to have one.
#     It is unregistered in rung 5, so nothing was relying on the name.
#   * `cpu-open-bus.nes` runs `Dummy write cycles` ($0407), not `Open Bus`
#     ($0408, which `open-bus.nes` runs). Already known -- `regress.sh` says so
#     in a comment and deliberately omits the ROM -- and now measured here too.
#   * `implied-dummy-reads.nes` and `implied-dummy-reads-v2.nes` are the same
#     test by every observable: same encoded index, same address, same verdict,
#     same settling frame. The `-v2` suffix records a rebuild, not a variant.
# TWO ROMS DO NOT PASS ON THE ORACLE and therefore cannot adjudicate the DUT --
# `subtest_verdict.py` refuses them by design. `sprite-eval-arbitrary-sprite-zero`
# (Fail(1) at $0458) was already recorded as deliberately unregistered;
# `sprite-zero-hit-behavior` (Fail(1) at $0457) is the same shape and is
# likewise absent from rung 5. Recorded rather than dropped: either the ROM
# does not stand alone or the entry needs the battery's preceding state, and
# both are open questions rather than DUT defects.
# NOTE ON THE LEGACY `ppu-misc-` PREFIX: several ROMs carry it while living on
# other pages (`ppu-misc-sprites-on-scanline-0` and
# `ppu-misc-stale-sprite-shift-regs` are Advanced Sprite Evaluation; `ale-read`
# and `hybrid-addresses` are Advanced BG Evaluation). The prefix is historical;
# the `entry` column is authoritative.
# `upstream_commit` is the AccuracyCoin commit the ROM was BUILT from. It is
# `legacy-unrecorded` for the 31 that predate this manifest -- and that is now
# a footnote rather than a gap, because the `result_addr` column pins what each
# ROM runs without it. What it still costs: a legacy ROM does not carry
# upstream's later fixes, and the two known ones are the `INC <ErrorCode`
# insertions (`TEST_MisalignedOAM2Addr` in `9bc42d1e`, `TEST_FrozenOAM2Inc2` in
# `46199ae4`). Neither routine is entered by any of the 31, so no failure code
# in this table is affected.
# RETRACTION, retained (46199ae4 re-sync). The v2.6.20 note here said the
# misaligned-oam2-address ROM was "built from the same `9bc42d1e` base, which
# PREDATES that upstream `INC`", and that is backwards: `9bc42d1e` is the
# commit that ADDED the `INC` to `TEST_MisalignedOAM2Addr`, so a ROM built at
# it INCLUDES the fix. The column was right and the prose was wrong. Settled
# by measurement rather than by reading, per this project's own rule: the
# committed ROM rebuilt byte-identically from `9bc42d1e`
# (md5 3e14c3d9a64070a3652a72503c4d34fb), which is also a standing
# demonstration that these builds are reproducible.
# Worth stating because this file exists to stop the next person guessing: a
# note that reads as settled and detailed is the one nobody re-derives.
# The one-byte relationship between the two v2.6.21 rows still holds and is
# MEASURED rather than asserted: the two builder outputs differ at exactly one
# offset, 0x10B5, 0x02 -> 0x03 (the `LDX #test` immediate; `LDY #suite` sits at
# REGENERATE WITH THE GENERATOR, AND THE SCHEMA LINE BELOW COMES FROM IT:
#   cargo run -p rustynes-test-harness --release --features test-roms \
#     --bin subtest_identify -- --tsv tests/roms/AccuracyCoin/sub-tests/*.nes
# Its output IS this file's data section, schema line included -- verified by
# regenerating and byte-comparing. The one column a measurement cannot supply is
# `upstream_commit`; pass `--upstream-commit <sha>` for a ROM whose build commit
# is known, or set it afterwards for the rows that have one (today, the two
# v2.6.21 rows). Anything the tool cannot identify it REFUSES to emit a row for,
# and says why on stderr.
